ai.description: *Hemidactylus chipkali* reaches 50 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a white belly. Key features include a flattened tail and unwebbed, leaf-shaped toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Hemidactylus chipkali* is the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, flattened tubercles along the flanks.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus chipkali* inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops in Central India, typically found at low to moderate elevations within scrubland and woodland habitats.
ai.behavior: The Central Indian Leaf-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt insects on vertical rock surfaces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus chipkali* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled, spherical eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus chipkali* is endemic to Central India, primarily inhabiting the states of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh within the Deccan Plateau biogeographic zone.
